model_annotation: This plot illustrates the performance (likely accuracy) of different methods across co-occurrence number groups for biomedical knowledge editing. The x-axis represents co-occurrence number groups, with four categorical tick labels: "<10¹", "[10¹, 10²)", "[10², 10³)", and "≥10³", arranged from left to right. The y-axis is labeled with a percentage symbol (%) and spans approximately from 30 to 65 on a linear scale, with tick marks visible at 55 and 60. Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different method: "Base" (appears as a gray or muted line), "FT" (fine-tuning), "IKE", "MEND", "MEMIT", and "ROME", as indicated in the legend at the top left. The "Base" line remains relatively flat across all groups at approximately 55%. The "FT" line stays low and relatively flat, around 33–35% across all groups. The "IKE" line is also relatively flat, hovering around 55–56%. The "MEND" line shows a slight decline from roughly 61% at "<10¹" to about 60% at "≥10³". The "MEMIT" line shows a more noticeable decline from approximately 63% at "<10¹" to around 60% at "≥10³". The "ROME" line starts highest at approximately 65% for the "<10¹" group and declines to roughly 62% at "≥10³". All editing method lines (MEND, MEMIT, ROME) exhibit a general downward trend as the co-occurrence number group increases, while Base, FT, and IKE remain comparatively stable across groups.
